title: O Come, O Come, Emmanuel
origin: Anonymous 15th-century French processional chant (VENI EMMANUEL), first printed in modern notation by Thomas Helmore in 1851

pd.detail: The tune VENI EMMANUEL is an anonymous 15th-century French Franciscan processional melody, in circulation for centuries before 1900; it was first printed in modern notation by Thomas Helmore in Part II of The Hymnal Noted, London, in the 1850s (sources date Part II variously to 1851 and 1854). Helmore died 1890.
pd.sourceEdition: Helmore's tune VENI EMMANUEL as it circulates in public-domain transcription: verified note for note and rhythm for rhythm against a Creative-Commons ABC setting in E minor (Paul Hardy's Christmas Tunebook, 4/4, quarter-note motion with three-beat phrase ends), with the opening independently confirmed against the Hymnary.org incipit for VENI EMMANUEL (13555 46543 45313), which matches the encoded pickup plus Verse A exactly.
pd.notes: This block covers the MUSIC only. The words are carried separately on each sung section with their own independent pd block: the anonymous Latin text of 1710, not J. M. Neale's English, which hymnals print in a heavily edited later revision. The tune is metricised the way hymnals set it rather than in free chant rhythm: even beats with three-beat holds at every phrase end. Meter was checked before encoding -- the consulted setting is barred in 4/4 throughout, so no compound-meter tune is being forced onto the grid. It is genuinely Aeolian - deg 7 (D natural) is never raised - so the validator's minor-key leading-tone warning is expected. The one-beat pickup is carried on the last beat of the preceding section, per the song book pickup rule. Verse A, Verse B and the Refrain are the source's own three strains, encoded note for note; the Refrain's last bar is a rest plus the pickup, added so the section is a whole 8 bars. The two-bar Intro is editorial: it is the tune's own cadence figure (4-2-1-7 / held 1) used as a lead-in, not extra tune.

pd.detail: The WORDS are an anonymous Latin metrical paraphrase of the medieval 'O' antiphons with no identifiable author, in circulation long before 1900 and first printed in Psalteriolum Cantionum Catholicarum, Koeln, 1710. The text is therefore free on its own dates, independently of the tune. The Latin original is carried rather than any English singing translation, so the words rest on the Latin text's own anonymous pre-1900 origin and not on a translator's dates.
pd.sourceEdition: Latin text as carried in 'Hymns of the Church: New and Old', 1912, no. 567 (p. 554), which prints all five Latin stanzas with the refrain and credits them to 'Anonymous, 12th cent.'; wording cross-checked against the 1710 Psalteriolum Cantionum Catholicarum reading.

lyrics.notes: Lines 1-2 of Latin stanzas 1 and 2. The Latin is Long Metre -- eight syllables a line -- and each line closes with a short melisma on its final syllable, which is why the phrase carries nine or ten notes for eight syllables. Line 1 is pinned to bar 0; its one-beat pickup is the last note of the Intro (beat 7), per the song book pickup rule. Line 2 is pinned to bar 3; its pickup is the note at beat 11, the last beat of bar 2. Two stanzas only: the three remaining stanzas of the 1710 printing are left unencoded rather than transcribed from memory. Nothing in this text is offensive and no stanza was dropped on those grounds.

lyrics.notes: Lines 3-4 of Latin stanzas 1 and 2 -- the second half of the same stanza whose first half sits on Verse A, since the source's four-line stanza is split across the two verse strains. Stanza numbering therefore matches Verse A: form entry Verse 1b sings stanza 1, Verse 2b sings stanza 2. Line 3 is pinned to bar 0; its pickup is the last beat of Verse A (beat 23 of that section). Line 4 is pinned to bar 3; its pickup is the note at beat 11, the last beat of bar 2. Two stanzas only, for the reason given on Verse A.

pd.sourceEdition: Latin refrain as carried in 'Hymns of the Church: New and Old', 1912, no. 567 (p. 554), where it is printed after every stanza and credited to 'Anonymous, 12th cent.'; wording cross-checked against the 1710 Psalteriolum Cantionum Catholicarum reading.

lyrics.notes: The refrain text is invariant in the source -- it is the same after every stanza -- so one stanza serves both Refrain Parts and no second set of words is needed. Line 1 is pinned to bar 0 and runs bars 0-3: the three-beat holds at beats 0 and 4 carry the two opening exclamations, then the descent closes on the held note in bar 3. Its pickup is the last beat of Verse B (beat 23 of that section). Line 2 is pinned to bar 4 and runs bars 4-6, landing on the four-beat hold at beat 24; its pickup is the note at beat 15, the last beat of bar 3. Bar 7 is the rest plus the pickup back into the next section and carries no words.
